content:
The Observatory says winds in Hong Kong will strengthen. At 8:10 pm, the government notified employees with long commutes to leave work, and reminded citizens who live in remote areas, have complicated journeys, or reside on outlying islands to start heading home.

On Saturday afternoon, the Strong Wind Signal No. 3 was in effect, and Typhoon Juju (Hong Kong transliteration of 紅霞) took the lead. Around 4 pm, the weather deteriorated and wind and rain began. At a construction site at 750 Cheung Sha Wan Road in Lai Chi Kok, a giant scaffolding collapsed in the wind and rain. The scaffolding, about five storeys high, toppled downward, with parts falling onto the roof of a nearby industrial building. Fire services dispatched a disaster response rescue vehicle and an ambulance to the scene, while police officers on site put on helmets and maintained order at a nearby bus stop. No injuries were reported initially.

During the typhoon, members of the public were seen buying vegetables and beef at Kowloon City Market, with long queues at the stalls. At a construction site, workers left the crane around 2 pm and returned to a safe location.

The Observatory said this afternoon that at 4 pm, Typhoon Juju was centred about 250 kilometres east-southeast of Hong Kong, moving at around 18 kilometres per hour. It is forecast to move northwest, generally tracking toward the coast of eastern Guangdong. The Observatory will assess whether it needs to issue a higher tropical cyclone warning signal between 9 pm and midnight, taking into account Juju's landfall location and distance from Hong Kong, the size of its area of gale-force winds, and local wind conditions.
